text:
Nora (CSM): quick weekly pulse for OrchidLabs — seeing a notable regression in batching/caching metrics: caching hit_rate ~18% (down from ~40%), avg_batch_size ~1.4, p95 latency ~240ms, error rate ~0.9% (retries up), and spend +18% week-over-week. cost_per_1k_tokens now approx $4.95. likely lots of tiny requests. any immediate mitigations to propose?

Sam (Success Eng): thanks Nora. can you share recent token-length distribution? also are these coming from a single API key / service?

Ria (Platform): pulled quick summary for last 48h — requests <64 tokens are 54% (baseline 30%). top caller is orchid-autoscale (high fanout).

Julian (Finance): that magnitude of small-request skew explains the spend delta. curious about options: increase batching window, enable auto-prefetch/prefix cache, or encourage client batching. need cost impact numbers for renewal deck.

Sam (Success Eng): operational experiment: two parallel canaries: 1) per-route batching.window_ms 20->45ms for orchid-autoscale 2) increase prefix_cache.ttl from 60s->300s for repeated prompt keys. run staging -> 5% prod -> 25% prod. tradeoff: small latency increase for single requests vs unit-cost drop.

Ria (Platform): current route config: `batching: {window_ms: 20, max_batch: 64, min_batch:1}` and `cache: {ttl_s: 60}`. I'll schedule canary and attach telemetry tag `orchid-mini-batch-03`. staging run in 20m. example deploy command:```bash
redwoodctl routes patch orchid-autoscale --data '{"batching":{"window_ms":45},"cache":{"ttl_s":300}}'
```

TelemBot: Alert: small_request_rate increased for route orchid-autoscale — small_rate=0.54, baseline=0.30, triggered=2026-03-22T14:05:12Z

Nora (CSM): good plan. Sam please own measurement (hit rate, batch avg, p95, errors, cost per 1k). Ria coordinate deploy and rollback. Julian will model cost scenarios. check back here after staging snapshot.

Sam (Success Eng): baseline capture: hit_rate=0.18, batch_size_avg=1.4, p95=240ms, errors=0.9%, cost_per_1k=$4.95. running staging canary now.

Ria (Platform): staging snapshot (45ms, ttl 300s): hit_rate=0.28, batch_size_avg=1.9, p95=255ms, errors=0.12%. staging looks stable. pushing 5% prod canary.

TelemBot: Deploy: route orchid-autoscale updated batching.window_ms 20->45, cache.ttl_s 60->300 at 2026-03-22T14:38:09Z by ria. canary=5%

Sam (Success Eng): prod 5% snapshot (first 30m): hit_rate=0.26, batch_size_avg=1.85, p95=248ms, errors=0.2%, cost_per_1k_est=$4.25. small but meaningful improvement.

Nora (CSM): thanks. let canary run full hour then expand to 25% if stable. logging this as `orchid-mini-batch-2026-03-22` for account notes. reduces near-term renewal risk if savings hold.

Julian (Finance): quick back-of-envelope: if we can sustain hit_rate ~0.26 and batch avg ~2.0 across traffic, unit cost falls to ~$3.65 per 1k tokens and monthly spend projection drops ~11%. will add to the renewal risk tracker.

Sam (Success Eng): final 5% canary (1h): hit_rate=0.30, batch_size_avg=2.05, p95=252ms, errors=0.18%, cost_per_1k_actual=$3.98. rolling to 25%.

Ria (Platform): 25% rollout done, monitoring. added telemetry tag `orchid-mini-batch-03` and a rollback script on standby.

Nora (CSM): excellent. next steps: - Sam/Ria validate 48h stability and then prepare PR to set new route defaults if safe. - Julian finalize cost delta for renewal deck. - Nora capture customer communication about recommended client-side batching best practices.

Sam (Success Eng): noted. I'll run a TTL-only test next week to isolate cache effect and also reach out to Orchid devs about client-side micro-batching as low-effort win.

Julian (Finance): will draft a short renewal note: projected monthly savings ~11% if rollouts stick. reduces renewal friction.

Ria (Platform): added quick runbook snippet for rollback:```bash
# rollback to previous settings
redwoodctl routes patch orchid-autoscale --data '{"batching":{"window_ms":20},"cache":{"ttl_s":60}}'
```

TelemBot: Info: canary telemetry tag orchid-mini-batch-03 added to traces starting 2026-03-22T14:38:09Z

Nora (CSM): thanks team. follow-up in 48h with stability numbers. tagging action owners: Sam (canary metrics), Ria (deploy/runbook), Julian (finance note). :white_check_mark:
